description: We are a  multidisciplinary team of aspiring software engineers, biotechnology engineers, graphic designers, and marketing professionals. Our name combines Mitochondrial Eve, symbolizing our shared biological origins, with “bits,” the basic units of computing. Together, we represent the connection between life and technology, combining our diverse skills to create innovative solutions and contribute to the future of science and technology in Nicaragua.
summary:
Eva-Bits is an offline-first precision agroecological mobile platform developed for smallholder farmers, guided by Eve, an empathetic virtual agronomist AI companion. Designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data), Eva-Bits eliminates the need for expensive ground IoT sensors by ingesting open-access NASA Earth observation data (POWER, SMAP, GPM, and MODIS/Landsat).

To address the challenge, our platform translates complex satellite telemetry, including root-zone soil moisture, precipitation, thermal accumulation (GDD), and solar irradiance, into clear, actionable field recommendations through deterministic biophysical modeling and spatial parcel graphs. Farmers receive crop rotation simulations, 7-day irrigation deficit schedules, optimal planting calendars, and early warnings for droughts and pests, operating seamlessly even without internet connectivity.

Eva-Bits is critical because intensifying climate extremes and severe droughts threaten smallholder food security and rural livelihoods. By democratizing satellite-driven precision agriculture at zero hardware cost, Eva-Bits empowers vulnerable communities to optimize scarce water and soil nutrients, adapt to climate volatility, and safeguard essential crop yields.
details:
Project Details: Eva-Bits

1. What does it do or how does it work?

Eva-Bits is an offline-first mobile platform that converts open-access NASA Earth observation data into actionable, plot-level agroecological management decisions for smallholder farmers. Guided by Eve, an empathetic virtual agronomist and phytopathologist avatar, the system works through a decoupled three-tier architecture:

  • Satellite Data Ingestion: Ingests daily NASA POWER agroclimatological feeds (temperature, solar radiation, relative humidity, precipitation), NASA SMAP L4 (root-zone and topsoil moisture), and NASA GPM IMERG (storm and rainfall tracking). It handles the typical 3–5 day satellite processing latency through a dynamic 7-day retrospective rolling window and localized historical baselines.
    1. Multi-Year Crop Rotation Simulator: Optimizes crop sequences to restore soil fertility and reduce synthetic fertilizer.
    2. 7-Day Dynamic Irrigation & Deficit Manager: Calculates daily crop evapotranspiration (ETaET_aETa​) against SMAP root moisture to pinpoint wilting points and water depth needs.
    3. Growing Degree Days (GDD) & Agricultural Calendar: Forecasts optimal planting windows and thermal accumulation.
    4. Crop Health & Foliar Vigor Monitor: Tracks canopy vigor and potential yield relative to historical norms.
    5. Flash Drought & Waterlogging Early Warning: Forecasts rapid moisture depletion or root asphyxiation 3 to 10 days in advance.
    6. Soil Nutritional Balance & Regeneration Score: Quantifies biological nitrogen fixation (BNF) and organic soil health.
  • Eve’s 21-Day Tri-Weekly Advisory: Synthesizes deterministic results into structured weekly milestones (Week 1: immediate moisture/pest control; Week 2: vegetative GDD tracking; Week 3: soil regeneration and harvest planning), accompanied by verifiable scientific citations.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Zero Hardware Investment: Completely replaces expensive, fragile IoT soil probes and ground weather stations by utilizing NASA satellite constellations.
  • 100% Offline Autonomy: Functions continuously in remote fields with zero cell service or Wi-Fi, storing all parcel graphs, calculations, and cached climate matrices locally in an encrypted SQLite database.
  • Water & Input Optimization: Prescribes soil-texture-specific irrigation techniques (e.g., high-frequency pulse drip, alternate furrow) that can reduce farm water usage by 35–40% and synthetic nitrogen dependence through planned legume rotations.
  • Extreme Weather Risk Mitigation: Gives smallholders proactive alerts to protect crops against flash droughts, heat waves during flowering, and soil waterlogging.
  • Inclusive & Frictionless Usability: Breaks technical barriers for farmers with limited digital or written literacy through voice-based natural language onboarding and intuitive visual cues.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Smallholder Climate Resilience: Protects vulnerable family farmers—particularly across the Central American Dry Corridor—against climate models' projected 24% decline in staple grain yields by 2030.
  • Democratizing Space Science: Translates complex NASA satellite telemetry into accessible, real-time farm practices for communities historically excluded from precision agriculture.
  • Agroecological Regeneration: Accelerates the transition from chemical-heavy monocultures to diversified, soil-restorative polycultures through biological nitrogen fixation and spatial pest barriers.
  • Food and Livelihood Security: Mitigates the risk of catastrophic harvest failures, stabilizing rural household incomes and local food supplies.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend & Mobile Core: Flutter 3.x and Dart 3.x (targeting Android and iOS).
  • Local Persistence & Graph Processing: SQLite (sqflite) for relational farm storage, spatial topology adjacency matrices, and offline caching.
  • Vector Graphics & Mascot Animation: Flutter CustomPainter rendering Eve’s 8-emote animated avatar at 60 FPS purely through code paths without heavy asset overhead.
  • Cloud & Serverless Microservices: Azure Functions (Python 3.10+) with RESTful JSON endpoints for automated satellite ingestion and caching.
  • AI Orchestration: Azure AI Foundry Studio (gpt-5-mini / GPT-4o) adhering to a strict source-grounding protocol.
  • NASA Earth Observations & APIs: NASA POWER Agroclimatology API (community=AG), NASA SMAP L4, NASA GPM IMERG, and MODIS/Landsat.
  • Development Environment: macOS, VS Code, Android Studio, Git/GitHub, and Mermaid.js.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Attributed Spatial Graph Modeling for Farms: Applying topological graph theory to rural parcel management allows the app to dynamically simulate downhill pesticide runoff, erosion risk, and beneficial ecological buffer zones between adjacent crops.
  • Deterministic Engine + Strict Source Grounding (Zero Hallucination): Instead of relying on generative AI to produce unverifiable numbers, all agronomic equations are computed deterministically. The AI companion (Eve) acts strictly as an empathetic translator and synthesizer, citing peer-reviewed agricultural science (CIAT, FAO, UNA).
  • Eve: The Vector-Animated Agronomist Avatar: Rather than presenting an intimidating spreadsheet or raw graphs, the farmer interacts with an animated companion equipped with 8 distinct, context-aware emotes (greeting, alert, sad, surprised, happy, thumbsUp, thumbsDown, pointing).
  • Conversational Onboarding with Vernacular Units: The intake engine parses natural spoken language and automatically normalizes traditional rural land measurements (such as Central American Manzanas and Tareas) into standardized hectares.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Rural Infrastructure Constraints: Designing with an uncompromising "Offline-First" principle because field connectivity in developing regions is virtually nonexistent.
  • NASA Satellite Data Latency: Overcoming the 3-to-5-day publication delay of NASA POWER by combining retrospective 7-day moving averages with local agroecological baseline matrices.
  • Cognitive Accessibility: Eliminating complex graphs and technical jargon in favor of clear 2.5D isometric plot visualizations, traffic-light alerts, and an optional visual avatar toggle for farmers who prefer a minimalist data display.
  • Scientific Rigor & Phytopathology: Grounding recommendations in validated regional agronomic literature spanning 13 key crops (maize, beans, coffee, melon, pineapple, etc.) to ensure field safety and farmer trust.
